Researcher session for issue #49 (delivery options and all-versions vs 2024-only effort). The report `docs/research/0002-delivery.md` is written, and the issue's verification command exits 0 (`missing: []`).

## Outputs
- `docs/research/0002-delivery.md`: the report. It has one section for each option (CLI text export, Python library, MCP server, committed text mirror). Each section covers how an agent uses the option, what it needs at runtime, offline and licensing limits, and which artifact families it can serve. It also has `## Effort: all versions vs 2024-only`, which gives effort ranges for each component and assumptions for each variant: core is 33–99 d for 2024-only and 89–264 d for all versions, the metadata-only tier is 5–14 d and 16–49 d, and wrapper costs are listed for each form. That section lists 8 version-format differences that drive the effort gap; each one cites a path under `@environment/pylavi/` or is marked [unverified]. The report also has `## Compatibility limits of the 2024 fallback` and `## Open measurements` (M1–M11).
- `docs/research/scripts/delivery/versions.py`: counts extensions, pylavi load results, `vers` and XML `LVVersion` values, and resource types.
- `docs/research/scripts/delivery/types_by_version.py`: groups resource types and `LVSR` flag-block size by saved major.minor version.

Run either script with `python3 -I <script> /resources/environment`. Both are read-only and offline, and they use only the prepared pylavi tree.

## Key findings
- pylavi loaded all 420 RSRC files in actor-framework, with 0 failures. It decodes metadata only (`vers`, `LVSR`, `BDPW`, paths). It does not decode the heaps (`BDHb`/`FPHb`) or `VCTP`/`LI*`.
- Saved versions are 20.0: 395 files, 21.0: 18, 24.1: 1, 24.3: 1. A 2024-only tool would not read 413 of 415 versioned files, including the fixture `Actor Core.vi` (`vers` 20.0.1f7).
- pylavi accepts only RSRC `format_version == 3` (`@environment/pylavi/pylavi/file.py`, `Header.VERSION`). Every observed `LVSR` flag block is 156 bytes. Formats older than 2020 cannot be measured with this corpus.
- The report states explicitly that it does not choose a delivery form or the fallback. That decision stays with the owner.

## Verification
`python3 -I -c "...req=['## Effort: all versions vs 2024-only','## Compatibility limits of the 2024 fallback','## Open measurements','MCP','CLI']..."` → exit 0, `missing: []`.

## What next
Nothing left for this issue. Next steps:
- The owner decides on a delivery form and the 2024 fallback, using this report.
- Later tasks can run the open measurements M1–M11 in the report. M1 (heap decodability) and M10 (`LVSR.version` vs `vers.version`) can run offline on the prepared sources.
